originality.rationale: The source supplies a closed-neighborhood conformity imitation probability, but its simulations update synchronously with interior payoff/conformity weights. Here the precisely defined asynchronous pure-conformity endpoint yields an all-initial-state exact star fixation law and quadratic leaf-seed asymptotics. The full motivating HTML text, including model, findings and appendix, was read. Min-San Miguel studies nonlinear copying and a graph-rewiring phase diagram; Castellano-Munoz-Pastor-Satorras treats mainly complete-graph q-voter; Katai-Urban-Pongracz-Szabo treats discordant push/pull star consensus-time. These mechanisms and statements do not, from inspected material, establish the claimed product and constant. Search of accessible published records found related star results with different rate rules or first-reversal events, not implication of this result. Related inaccessible full texts remain a documented nonzero historical-priority risk.
residual_risks: Two closely related indexed results were available only as summaries and may contain uninspected stronger statements.
Broader q-voter star or absorbing-chain results could independently derive this exact formula; novelty is literature-bounded.
The source parent excludes the pure-conformity endpoint and uses synchronous updating, so interpretation is limited to the newly defined variant.

value.rationale: The parent literature identifies the interaction of conformity and heterogeneous network hubs but does not quantify a lone seed effect. Here a cooperative hub retains positive limiting fixation while a leaf loses influence quadratically, versus the ordinary voter law of linear decline. That exponent change is a structural, nontrivial boundary demonstrating how local majority imitation alters spatial influence, and the all-state product supports further calculations of seeding and network interventions. The result has natural object/invariant motivation rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
